title: A negative inaccurate universal half-allocation attempt
statement: The preserved shared_mode_universal.py allocates one half of covariance to each local triad, uses the retained four-wave data and Young bounds for quartic interactions, and seeks a positive gap through floating-point Hessian-energy upper bounds and a PSD-plus-nonnegative remainder. After replacing the missing cubic_target_vectors key with cubic_targets, the producer run reports status optimal_inaccurate and gap -2.4056995211233407, with a solver-inaccuracy warning. The initial KeyError is a corrected source-interface error; the later negative numerical gap is a separate preliminary mathematical-search outcome. Neither proves the proposed allocation exactly infeasible, rules out better allocations or certifies a general shared-mode obstruction.

requires: Retained F_star/acoustic and cubic-coordinate helpers and the existing overlap certificate; two local triads on four shared wave directions

Universal proposal uses fourth ray (1,1/2;1/2,1/4), half covariance per local triad and a Young-inequality bound for quartets; literal floating-point PSD-plus-entrywise-nonnegative sufficient-cone formulation

Ordering proposal rescales the fourth ray to (4,2;2,1), rescales the second cubic target by four and uses 24 permutation charts with chart-dependent minimum allocations; its raw gap values have this distinct normalization

Only preserved supplied source bytes and visible source-relevant outputs are used. Initial cubic_target_vectors key error and correction to cubic_targets remain explicit; no scientific script is rerun

assumptions: Active-turn preliminary floating-point proposals only. The universal half-allocation solve is optimal_inaccurate with a negative gap; ordering charts include negative gaps. Neither is an exact certificate of infeasibility, a general impossibility result, a full-face proof or a counterexample to the prior restricted gluing theorems. Positive chart gaps are also not exact all-chart certificates. Independent overlapping amplitudes, unrestricted resonance networks and global quasiconvexity of the original 28D face remain unresolved. The arbitrary-amplitude triad, fixed-relative-amplitude overlapping block, their distinct separated-block conditions, earlier exclusions and immutable versions remain intact. No independent scientific audit, new novelty claim, practical advantage or physical interpretation is established.
costs: Source scripts use NumPy, SciPy, CVXPY and CLARABEL, floating eigendecompositions with negative eigenvalues clipped to zero in square-root factors, numerical Hessian-cost upper bounds and PSD/nonnegative sufficient decompositions
